key_insight: A particle-based simulation shows that dense suspensions of granular spherocylinders exhibit a startup viscosity spike and then settle into steady viscosities that grow with both solids volume fraction and particle aspect ratio.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict and tune the flow behavior of rod-shaped particulate slurries used in manufacturing and natural granular suspensions.
method: Simulates spherocylindrical rods under simple shear flow.
Includes short-range frictional contact and hydrodynamic lubrication forces.
Uses new lubrication-force schemes and dynamic timestep control.
evidence_signal: The model is compared against the limited available experimental rheology data and reproduces observed trends in viscosity and particle alignment.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on simulations for aspect ratios up to 20 and on limited experimental validation, so performance outside this range or for different contact models may need further checking.
paper_title: Rheology of dense suspensions of granular spherocylinders by particle-based simulation
